instructorNote: Show the dashboard. A minute later, read the preschool director's call aloud (she smells gas and has 22 children and 4 staff, and her drill sends them to the church parking lot inside the gas zone; Little Acorn has children in the play yard). Then read the print shop manager at the fence (14 people at the presses) and say that Valley Gas is about half an hour out and Dayton Fire has no arrival time yet. Watch for three things: the Superintendent evacuates the print shop, apartment house, preschool and play yard on Larkspur's own authority, sets a new muster point upwind and more than 300 feet away, and hands the evacuation to Fire when they arrive; the EOR reads the CG-3 trend and gives a structural opinion without declaring a building status; and the Safety Director notifies the building official, Fiona Castellanos. This is the first decision point: the superintendent must choose who moves and where, before Fire arrives.
